Troubleshooting

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/troubleshooting.Rmd
troubleshooting.Rmd

Version Problems

In order to follow the examples in this documentation site, you should have the latest version of plotly.core installed (0.1.0), as detailed in the Getting Started guide. These pages are written for plotly.core, which is a different package from the legacy plotly R package: code written for plotly (plot_ly(), layout(), subplot(), …) will not work here, and vice versa. plotly.core bundles its own copy of the Plotly.js rendering engine, so figures look the same wherever they are rendered. Read on for details about troubleshooting plotly.core in other environments such as Dash.

Import Problems

Most loading problems can be traced back to having multiple or outdated versions of plotly.core installed. It’s often worthwhile to uninstall before following the Getting Started instructions from scratch. You can run the following commands in the console to fully remove plotly.core before installing again:

remove.packages('plotly.core')

Problems can also arise if you have a file named plotly.core.R in the same directory as the code you are executing.

Dash Problems

If you are encountering problems using plotly.core with Dash please first ensure that you have upgraded dash to the latest version, which will automatically upgrade dash-core-components to the latest version, ensuring that Dash is using an up-to-date version of the Plotly.js rendering engine. If this does not resolve your issue, please visit our Dash Community Forum and we will be glad to help you out.

This is an example of a plotly.core graph inside dash: 

library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_bar(x = c(0, 1, 2), y = c(3, 7, 9))
#fig

library(dash)
library(dashCoreComponents)
library(dashHtmlComponents)

app <- Dash$new()

app$layout(
  htmlDiv(
    list(
      dccGraph(
        id = "graph",
        figure = fig
      )
    )
  )
)

#app$run_server()

Use app$run_server() to run the dash app.

Static Image Export Problems

plotly.core does not use the orca executable. save_image() exports figures with headless Chrome (driven by the chromote package). If export fails because no browser is found, set the CHROMOTE_CHROME environment variable to the complete path of a Chrome or Chromium-based browser, or download Chrome Headless Shell once with chromote::chrome_versions_add("latest-stable", "chrome-headless-shell"). See Static Image Export for details.
